headline: A 2017 executive order added more US sanctions related to North Korea.
what_it_does: This order, signed by President Trump on September 20, 2017, added to the sanctions the United States already had on North Korea. Sanctions are rules that limit trade, money transfers, or business with a country and with people or companies tied to it. No summary was provided, so the exact details of who is targeted and how are not described here.

who_it_affects.group: People and companies doing business with or in North Korea
who_it_affects.how: They may face new US penalties, such as having their US-held property frozen or being cut off from dealing with Americans.
They may need to follow new rules that bar dealings with people or groups named under the order.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed September 20, 2017; the exact effective date is not stated in the provided material.
